topic.title: Mathematical Reasoning and Verifier-Guided Proof Search
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: This topic connects mathematical problem solving with tools that can check whether a proposed argument is valid. Methods learn to select useful premises, generate proof steps, search alternatives, and revise failed attempts using formal feedback. Evaluation also asks whether apparent progress reflects new reasoning or memorization of publicly available problems.
topic.whyItMatters: Formal verification can turn a plausible-looking answer into a checkable result, although finding that result may require substantial computation. Fresh competition problems and proof-writing tasks expose different capabilities from familiar short-answer benchmarks, making evaluation design part of the research problem.
topic.evolution: DeepMath in 2016 applies neural sequence models to premise selection on formal mathematics. Later representatives combine language generation with grounded proofs and Lean collaboration. MathArena in 2025 evaluates newly released competition problems, while a 2026 approach uses compiler failure categories to guide local corrections without retaining an ever-growing history of proof attempts.
openQuestions: How can verifier feedback reduce search cost on genuinely new mathematical domains?
What evaluations measure proof quality without rewarding benchmark contamination?

papers.tldr: ConvexBench exposes failures in recognizing convexity under deep composition and shows that external parsing plus recursive reasoning can substantially improve performance.

papers.title: DecAEvolve: Decompose, Adapt, and Evolve for Effective LLM-based Scientific Equation Discovery
papers.tldr: DecAEvolve combines symbolic term feedback with test-time reinforcement learning to improve the accuracy and efficiency of scientific equation discovery.

papers.title: Decompose, Structure, and Repair: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Autoformalization via Operator Trees
papers.tldr: DSR organizes mathematical statements into operator trees to guide formal translation and targeted error repair.

papers.title: Differentiable Conformal Training for LLM Reasoning Factuality
papers.tldr: A differentiable factuality filter learns to retain more reasoning claims while preserving conformal reliability guarantees.

papers.title: Draft-and-Audit Reinforcement Learning for Optimization Modeling
papers.tldr: Draft-and-Audit RL trains a shared policy to write and revise optimization programs using rewards from only the final audited execution.

papers.title: Editable Proof Sketch for Automated Theorem Proving
papers.tldr: EditableSketch lets theorem-proving systems revise proof plans locally while preserving completed subgoals, reducing cost and improving reported performance.

papers.title: Efficient Numeracy in Language Models through Single-Token Number Encodings
papers.tldr: BitTokens encodes numbers as single tokens using floating-point bits, enabling small language models to learn nearly perfect basic arithmetic.

papers.title: Enhancing Neural Theorem Proving via High-Quality Data Selection and Verifier Feedback
papers.tldr: Selecting diverse, informative Isabelle proofs and incorporating verifier feedback raises reported miniF2F-test performance to 90.6% Pass@64.

papers.title: Euclean: Automated Geometry Problem Formalization with Unified Verification in Lean
papers.tldr: Euclean formalizes geometry directly in Lean’s Mathlib and produces large training datasets that improve downstream proof success.

papers.title: Evaluating Robustness of Reasoning Models on Parameterized Logical Problems
papers.tldr: A parameterized 2-SAT benchmark reveals abrupt reasoning failures caused by logical structure that aggregate accuracy can hide.

papers.title: ExVerus: Verus Proof Repair via Counterexample Reasoning
papers.tldr: ExVerus turns validated counterexamples into guidance for repairing Verus proofs, improving reported accuracy, robustness, and token efficiency.

papers.title: Faults in Our Formal Benchmarking: Dataset Defects and Evaluation Failures in Lean Theorem Proving
papers.tldr: An audit of Lean benchmarks shows that specification defects and evaluation failures can distort scores despite machine-checked proofs.

papers.title: FormalRx: Rectify and eXamine Semantic Failures in Autoformalization
papers.tldr: FormalRx diagnoses mathematical autoformalization failures by classifying, locating, and correcting semantic errors.

papers.title: From LLM-Generated Conjectures to Lean Formalizations: Automated Polynomial Inequality Proving via Sum-of-Squares Certificates
papers.tldr: NSPI turns language-model proposals for polynomial sum-of-squares decompositions into exact certificates and Lean-checked inequality proofs.

papers.title: FrontierCS: Evolving Challenges for Evolving Intelligence
papers.tldr: FrontierCS uses objectively scored, open-ended programming problems to reveal a substantial gap between frontier models and human experts.

papers.title: GaussTrace: Provenance Analysis of 3D Gaussian Splatting Models with Evidence-based LLM Reasoning
papers.tldr: GaussTrace combines parameter statistics, simulated edits, and language-model reasoning to infer provenance relationships among 3D Gaussian Splatting assets.

papers.title: HERMES: Towards Efficient and Verifiable Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
papers.tldr: Hermes interleaves informal mathematical reasoning with Lean verification, improving evaluated accuracy while reducing inference cost.

papers.title: HiPhO: How Far Are (M)LLMs from Humans in the Latest High School Physics Olympiad Benchmark?
papers.tldr: HiPhO uses official physics Olympiad grading and medal thresholds to compare 30 models with human contestants.

papers.title: How Powerful are LLMs in Generating Formal Program Specifications?
papers.tldr: Coins evaluates generated formal specifications through trusted test cases and concrete proofs, helping separate specification quality from proof difficulty.

papers.title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
papers.tldr: Single-prover interactive proofs can support oracle-aided verification when the computation tolerates oracle errors or the oracle has low-degree polynomial structure.

papers.title: HypoSpace: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Set-Valued Hypothesis Generation under Underdetermination and Sublinear Coverage Bounds
papers.tldr: HypoSpace reveals that LLMs can generate valid hypotheses while covering only a shrinking share of the admissible alternatives.

papers.title: INDUCTION: Finite-Structure Concept Synthesis in First-Order Logic
papers.tldr: INDUCTION evaluates logical rule discovery in finite worlds and finds that compact formulas generalize substantially better than bloated ones.

papers.title: Inference-Time Conformal Reasoning with Valid Factuality Control for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: ITCR calibrates graph-level factual uncertainty during reasoning generation to determine when to stop, with theoretical and empirical coverage support.

papers.title: Influence-Guided Symbolic Regression: Scientific Discovery via LLM-Driven Equation Search with Granular Feedback
papers.tldr: IGSR guides language-model equation search with term-level influence scores and reports a biological hypothesis supported by wet-lab experiments.

papers.title: InteractScience: Programmatic and Visually-Grounded Evaluation of Interactive Scientific Demonstration Code Generation
papers.tldr: InteractScience combines functional tests and visual assessment to reveal gaps in models’ ability to build interactive scientific demonstrations.

papers.title: Judging What We Cannot Solve: A Consequence-Based Approach for Oracle-Free Evaluation of Research-Level Math
papers.tldr: Consequence-Based Utility ranks research-math solutions by how much they help solve related, verifiable questions.

papers.title: LECTOR: Joint Optimization of Scientific Reasoning Graphs and Introduction Generation
papers.tldr: LECTOR jointly improves an evidence-grounded reasoning graph and its written introduction to strengthen scientific logic, citations, and consistency.

papers.title: LLM-MatLogic: Executable Exchange Contracts for Knowledge-Graph Query Answering with Scoped Negation
papers.tldr: LLM-MatLogic makes exclusion scope executable so knowledge-graph queries enforce negative conditions on the intended branches and evidence paths.

papers.title: MathlibLemma: Folklore Lemma Generation and Benchmark for Formal Mathematics
papers.tldr: MathlibLemma mines missing reusable mathematical facts, producing checked Lean proofs and a benchmark of formal statements.

papers.title: miniF2F-Dafny: LLM-Guided Mathematical Theorem Proving via Auto-Active Verification
papers.tldr: miniF2F-Dafny shows that automated verification can solve many benchmark theorems unaided, with LLM guidance improving the best reported result to 62.7% pass@4.

papers.title: MOOSE-Star: Unlocking Tractable Training for Scientific Discovery by Breaking the Complexity Barrier
papers.tldr: MOOSE-Star decomposes hypothesis generation and structures inspiration search to enable scalable training, with logarithmic complexity in the best case.

papers.title: Numina-Lean-Agent: An Open and General Agentic Reasoning System for Formal Mathematics
papers.tldr: Numina-Lean-Agent connects a general coding agent to Lean tools, solving all 12 Putnam 2025 problems and supporting collaborative theorem formalization.

papers.title: Open-World LLM Logical Reasoning
papers.tldr: OpenIKLR combines logical solvers and language models to detect missing premises, propose additions, and check their logic and factual accuracy.

papers.title: OPT-Engine: Benchmarking the Limits of LLMs in Optimization Modeling via Complexity Scaling
papers.tldr: OPT-Engine scales optimization-task complexity and identifies constraint formulation as the key bottleneck for solver-integrated language-model reasoning.

papers.title: Opt-Verifier: Unleashing the Power of LLMs for Optimization Modeling via Dual-Side Verification
papers.tldr: OptiVer improves language-model-generated optimization formulations by checking both their structure and the validity of their solutions.

papers.title: Pessimistic Verification for Open-Ended Math Questions
papers.tldr: Parallel flaw detection and fine-grained proof decomposition improve reported mathematical verification accuracy and token efficiency.

papers.title: Position: LLM for Physics Research Requires Domain-Specialized Training and Tooling
papers.tldr: The authors argue that useful physics research agents require specialized training and verification tools grounded in physical principles.

papers.title: Position: Mathematical DSL Benchmarks Need Executable Interface Contracts
papers.tldr: A JGEX dataset and conformance audit show why mathematical benchmarks need documentation backed by versioned execution and runnable examples.

papers.title: Position: Theory-Level Autoformalization, From Isolated Statements to Unified Formal Knowledge Bases
papers.tldr: Autoformalization should build connected formal theories, including their definitions and dependencies, rather than focus only on individual statements.

papers.title: PPDL: LLM-Based Flows as Probabilistic Programs
papers.tldr: PPDL represents language-model workflows as probabilistic programs that propagate uncertainty and support inference-scaling experiments from the same flow logic.

papers.title: ProOPF: Benchmarking and Improving LLMs for Professional-Grade Power Systems Optimization Modeling
papers.tldr: ProOPF supplies executable training examples and expert-annotated tests for translating operational requests into power-system optimization models.

papers.title: Protein Design with Agent Rosetta: A Case Study for Specialized Scientific Agents
papers.tldr: Agent Rosetta combines an LLM with a structured software environment to perform broad protein-design tasks at competitive quality.

papers.title: QEDBench: Quantifying the Alignment Gap in Automated Evaluation of University-Level Mathematical Proofs
papers.tldr: QEDBench finds systematic gaps between LLM proof grading and expert assessment, including inflated scores and strong domain-dependent weaknesses.

papers.title: Reasoning Structure of Large Language Models
papers.tldr: A logic-puzzle benchmark turns reasoning traces into verifiable dependency graphs, exposing behavioral differences hidden by accuracy and token counts.

papers.title: Scaling Generative Verifiers For Natural Language Mathematical Proof Verification And Selection
papers.tldr: Combined generative verifiers perform best in the study, but improved proof metrics do not necessarily improve final-answer precision.

papers.title: Scientific logicality enriched methodology for LLM reasoning: A practice in physics
papers.tldr: This work uses logicality assessment and data selection to improve language models’ scientific reasoning, demonstrated through physics.

papers.title: SEDRAS: Symbolically Evaluated Deep Research And Science
papers.tldr: SEDRAS tests model-generated scientific theories against synthetic ground truth and finds pronounced weaknesses in choosing informative observations.

papers.title: SL-VC: A Benchmark and Automated Framework for Separation Logic Verification Condition Proving
papers.tldr: SL-VC exposes difficulties in separation-logic proof synthesis, while SPLIT improves results through specialized tactics and staged reasoning.

papers.title: SorryDB: Can AI Provers Complete Real-World Lean Theorems?
papers.tldr: SorryDB supplies continuously updated real-world Lean tasks and finds that current proving approaches have complementary strengths.

papers.title: Towards Diverse Scientific Hypothesis Search with Large Language Models
papers.tldr: EvoDiverse searches across interacting temperature levels to produce higher-quality, more diverse scientific hypotheses within a fixed validation budget.

papers.title: Towards Professional-Grade Financial Agents: Benchmarking, Tooling, and Structured Reasoning
papers.tldr: ProFinAgent combines financial tools, graph-based planning, and case memory, reporting improved performance and lower latency on financial reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Towards Solving the Gilbert-Pollak Conjecture via Large Language Models
papers.tldr: An LLM-guided system generates verifiable geometric lemmas and raises the certified Steiner-ratio lower bound to 0.8559.

papers.title: VeriSimpl: Robust Optimization Modeling from Natural Language using Simplification-based Verification
papers.tldr: VeriSimpl uses solver-generated simplified questions to help LLMs verify that optimization formulations match their natural-language descriptions.

papers.title: Why Agentic Theorem Prover Works: A Statistical Provability Theory of Mathematical Reasoning Models
papers.tldr: A theory of budgeted proof success links learned-prover errors to visited states, proof length, training coverage, and conditional improvements from action-value separation.

papers.title: XDomainBench: Diagnosing Reasoning Collapse in High-Dimensional Scientific Knowledge Composition
papers.tldr: XDomainBench tests interactive scientific reasoning across disciplines and reveals reported collapse driven by composition difficulty and interaction-amplified errors.
